recommendation_issues.problem: Sound and the most compact option checked, but it understates the own code. A typed fetch helper needs one typed route table in packages/contracts (method, path, request and response schemas) that the server also registers its routes from; without it, paths and types drift and no generation step catches it. Client response types must be the wire form: the type provider serializes responses from z.output since v7, so response schemas must not contain transforms or codecs (Zod's JSON Schema conversion throws on z.date() and transforms by default, which helps enforce this).

Premature. Switching now means taking @fastify/type-provider-zod 1.0.0, its only release (2026-04-19), while the fixes it ported from upstream on 2026-09-10 (#29) are in no release yet. The 'Core plugin' argument is false (see correction). Make it conditional: start on fastify-type-provider-zod 7.0.0 pinned (same exports), move the import path to @fastify/type-provider-zod once it publishes a release containing #29. Dropping fastify-zod-openapi and naming the zero-dependency setValidatorCompiler/setSerializerCompiler fallback is sound.

--throw-deprecation throws on every deprecation in the process (Node core and every dependency), not only FSTDEP codes, so a deprecation inside pg, pino, Better Auth or a Node 26 change can turn CI red outside the developer's control. Keep the flag, exempt known third-party codes one by one with --disable-warning=<code> and record each exemption in the plan.

Adding Better Auth's openAPI plugin to the production auth instance exposes GET /open-api/generate-schema to anyone; disableDefaultReference only turns off /reference. Generate the auth document in CI from a test-only auth configuration that adds the plugin, and keep the plugin out of the production config. Moving basePath under /v1 is optional; the oasdiff check works at /api/auth as well.

A device-keyed limit is only safe if the device id is authenticated before the limiter runs. @fastify/rate-limit runs in onRequest by default, where a device id is an unverified claim that a client can rotate. Run that limiter in the preHandler hook after device authentication and keep a wide IP limit in onRequest as a flood guard. The finding also fixes only Fastify's view of the client IP; Better Auth needs the same address handed in (high miss below).

Better Auth's database storage keeps per-client counters only if Better Auth can resolve the client IP. Under the plan's Fastify integration it cannot, so the table would hold one shared bucket per path. Accept only together with the IP fix in the high miss.

Biome noRestrictedImports matches import specifier strings with gitignore-style patterns, so it has no equivalent of dependency-cruiser's $1 back reference; as a fallback it needs one override block per module or path aliases such as @modules/<name>. misses.finding: Better Auth never sees the client address. The Fastify integration the plan links builds a Fetch Request from request.headers only, so neither the socket IP nor Fastify's trustProxy result reaches Better Auth. Better Auth 1.7.7 reads x-forwarded-for by default; in production, with no such header, getIP returns null and the rate limiter falls back to one shared bucket per path, logging a single warning. Its default special rules allow 3 requests per 60 s on /email-otp/send-verification-otp and 3 per 10 s on /sign-in paths, which then apply to every instructor at once. The plan's Compose (line 714) has no proxy in front, so this is the as-written state: logins fail under ordinary load at term start, and one anonymous client sending 3 requests a minute locks every instructor out of code requests (lines 69, 586). The reverse case also fails: a single client-supplied X-Forwarded-For value is accepted without trustedProxies, so an attacker rotates it to dodge the strict limit on code endpoints. S02-07 fixed only Fastify's side, and S02-08's database storage would just persist the shared bucket.

misses.finding: Line 729 promises one short transaction per submission and line 592 enqueues jobs in the same transaction, yet a submission crosses modules (yoklama needs data owned by oturumlar and listeler, plus the device record, which the plan does not assign to yoklama). If a public face uses the pool-level db instead of the caller's tx, its query runs outside the transaction (no rollback, cannot see uncommitted rows) and checks out a second connection. With node-postgres defaults (max 10, connectionTimeoutMillis 0, FIFO wait), ten concurrent submissions that each hold one connection and wait for a second never finish, which is exactly the class-exit load. The plan states neither a tx-passing rule for public faces nor a pool wait limit.

verdict_reason: No high-severity finding is refuted or unverifiable: S02-01 (openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch end of life) is confirmed, with extra evidence that openapi-typescript pins TypeScript ^5.x against the plan's TypeScript 6. Two findings are corrected: S02-02's 'Core plugin' claim is false and switching to the official fork now is premature; S02-12 missed that oasdiff treats a new response enum value as ERR. One high-severity miss remains: under the plan's own Fastify integration Better Auth cannot see client IPs and falls back to a shared per-path bucket (3 code requests per minute for all instructors, lockable by one anonymous client), which S02-07 and S02-08 did not catch. Two further misses: public faces must take the caller's transaction (medium) and the batch body limit (low).
